title: Run a content pipeline
summary: Turn making content from a scramble into a repeatable pipeline: capture ideas, batch the work, check quality, repurpose and review. Process, not promises.
audience: Anyone who wants to publish regularly without burning out.
disclaimer: Education only. Keep what you publish accurate, credit your sources and respect copyright and platform rules.

modules.title: Capture and plan
modules.goal: Never start from a blank page.

steps.title: Start an idea bank
steps.why: Ideas arrive at random times. A single place to catch them means you pick from a list instead of staring at a blank screen.
do: Choose one place (a note, a document) as your only idea inbox.
Add ten ideas today, each as a one-line headline with who it is for.

prompts.label: Fill the bank
prompts.text: My topic is <topic> and my audience is <audience>. Give me 20 specific content ideas as one-line headlines, grouped by: teach, show, answer a question, tell a story. Remove anything generic.

tips: Keep the ones that make you curious.
steps.check: Your idea bank has at least ten entries.

steps.title: Plan a month on one page
steps.why: A visible plan turns 'what do I make today' into 'what is next on the list'.
do: Pick a realistic cadence you can keep (less than you think).
Place ideas on a month calendar, mixing easy and hard.

prompts.label: Draft a calendar
prompts.text: Plan a four-week content calendar publishing <cadence>, using these ideas: <ideas>. Alternate easy and effortful pieces and leave one slot a week free.

tips: A slower schedule you keep beats a fast one you drop.
Leave a free slot for what happens in the world.

modules.title: Make, check, reuse
modules.goal: A pipeline with quality checks and reuse built in.

steps.title: Batch the work
steps.why: Doing the same kind of task together (all scripts, then all recording) saves setup time and keeps quality even.
do: Make three pieces in one sitting by stage: outline, draft, polish.

prompts.label: Outline in bulk
prompts.text: Turn each of these three ideas into a structured outline (hook, three key points, one example, call to action): <ideas>. Keep each to ten lines.

tips: Stop each stage while it is still easy to start again.
steps.check: You produced three outlines or drafts in one session.

steps.title: Add a checklist before anything goes out
steps.why: A short checklist catches the mistakes you only see after publishing: facts, names, links, tone and permissions.
do: Write a ten-line checklist for your work.
Run your next piece through it before publishing.

prompts.label: Draft the checklist
prompts.text: Write a pre-publish checklist (ten items) for <type of content>: facts and sources checked, names spelled right, links work, nothing private shown, permissions for images and music, claims I can back up, tone matches my audience.

tips: If you are unsure of a fact, leave it out or say you are unsure.
steps.check: Your checklist exists and you used it once.

steps.title: Repurpose one piece four ways
steps.why: One good piece can become several honest, smaller ones, each suited to where it is read or watched.
do: Make a short summary, three quotes or tips, a question for your audience, and a next-step link.

prompts.label: Repurpose
prompts.text: Here is my finished piece: <text>. Make: a 50-word summary, three short tips, one question to ask my audience, and a one-line description. Keep my meaning, do not add claims.

tips: Say where it came from; do not pretend each is brand new.
steps.check: One piece became at least four smaller ones.
